additions.name: BONC Horinger Intelligent Computing Centre — existing operations

status.summary: On 10 August 2026 the Horinger New Area Party-Mass Service Center published on the New Area management committee's website that the BONC (东方国信) Horinger intelligent computing centre currently serves customers. Its customers cover research institutions and AI service providers, and its orders for domestic customised compute are growing steadily. The item also gives a CNY 4.8 billion total investment and a plan for more than 100,000 P of intelligent compute. This present-tense government statement supports current operation of the existing base as of the publication date. It names no building or phase. The August 2025 substation EIA says Phase 1 has operated since 2025 and Phase 2 is under construction. Completion or operation of Phase 2, and the planned capacity, are not asserted.

locator.precision: EIA station-centre point of the campus's planned 2# 110 kV substation, which the report places in the central-east of the BONC Industrial Internet Northern Regional Center plant area (about 13.1 ha). It locates the campus through on-campus support infrastructure. It is not an operating data-centre building, a parcel centroid, an entrance or the construction extent.
locator.identity_review: The report form, accepted by the Hohhot EEB on 26 August 2025, names the 2# 110 kV substation of Phase 2 of the BONC Industrial Internet Northern Regional Center (东方国信工业互联网北方区域中心). It is built by Inner Mongolia BONC Technology Co., Ltd. in the Yungu area of Horinger New Area, inside the campus's plant area with no new land take. The printed point 111°48'38.413" E, 40°32'31.242" N was transcribed arithmetically. It agrees within 1.44 m with the centroid of the report's own CGCS2000 3-degree Gauss-Kruger (CM 111E) corner coordinates of the 49 x 23.5 m substation footprint, so it reads as CGCS2000 (WGS84 to well under a metre). In Esri World Imagery the point falls in the central-east of a road-bounded block. Built data halls stand in the block's west part and a residential compound adjoins it to the east, matching the report's 克略和苑 compound 62 m east of the substation. The block is separated by an east-west road from the China Mobile Hohhot data-centre block to the south-east. The supply-line EIA puts the cable terminals of the campus's first own 110 kV substation about 310 m west-north-west, at the campus's north side south of Shuju Street. The New Area's 'BONC Horinger intelligent computing centre' is identified with this campus as follows. BONC's homepage describes a single 'Inner Mongolia Horinger intelligent computing base'. The EIA describes this campus as BONC's Horinger compute campus, with intelligent-computing cabinets of 10.8-24 kW. No other BONC project appears in the Hohhot EEB EIA lists (2023 to October 2026), the Inner Mongolia EEB publicity lists (September 2025 to October 2026) or the New Area news lists. Details: sources/research-countries-2026-10-23-cn-north-p2-bonc-horinger-geometry-facts.json.
locator.uncertainty_reason: No survey accuracy is stated. The datum and transcription are checked by the 1.4 m agreement with the report's CGCS2000 corner coordinates. The point marks the planned 2# substation, not the operating Phase 1 buildings; its offset from them is unknown but within the campus, which extends a few hundred metres around the point. Decimal places are transcription precision, not accuracy.

additions.name: China Mobile Hohhot Data Center — existing intelligent computing centre operations
additions.site_identity_review: The China Mobile intelligent computing centre in Horinger New Area belongs to the existing China Mobile Hohhot Data Center campus; it is not a new site. The Hohhot DRC item of 15 October 2026 says the campus's B25/B27 project, the existing Atlas project, adds to 'the world's largest single operator intelligent computing centre'. The New Area items of 10 and 27 August 2026 call the China Mobile Hohhot (liquid-cooled) intelligent computing centre the world's largest single liquid-cooled intelligent computing centre among operators. The only Atlas project on this campus is the B25/B27 expansion (completed 10 October 2026). The operating centre described in August, before B25/B27 completed, is a separate project on the same site.

status.summary: On 27 August 2026 the Horinger New Area administrative approval bureau reported that guests on the 23 August industry tour visited the China Mobile intelligent computing centre. The bureau describes it as the world's largest single liquid-cooled operator intelligent computing centre, which has deployed about 20,000 AI accelerator cards (over 89% domestic chips) with up to 6.7 EFLOPS of intelligent compute. The New Area's 10 August 2026 item, attached as context, says the China Mobile Hohhot liquid-cooled intelligent computing centre has 6.7 EFLOPS in total. It also says the centre has run a 10,000-card cluster for 22 days of uninterrupted training, with 86% direct green power and a machine-room PUE as low as 1.15. These present-tense government statements support operation of the existing intelligent computing centre as of 27 August 2026. They name no buildings. The B25/B27 expansion, still under construction then and completed on 10 October 2026, is a separate project and is not included.

locator.identity_review: This reuses the existing campus point, a representative point inside the community-mapped named China Mobile Hohhot Data Center parent campus, with its pinned evidence and unchanged uncertainty. The point locates the parent campus. It does not identify the buildings of the operating intelligent computing centre. The baseline B25/B27 project has no geometry-identity evidence, so none is pinned.

additions.name: Echelon DUB10 — operating data-centre installation (Energy Centre and data centre buildings; build-out continuing)

status.summary: Echelon's DUB10 Noise Management Plan (version 1.0, issued 21 September 2026), submitted to the EPA under IE licence P1113-02 on 28 September 2026 and posted to LEAP on 22 October 2026, states that 'The licensed installation operates on a continuous basis and comprises the DUB10 Energy Centre, associated data centre buildings and supporting infrastructure' at Crag Avenue, Clondalkin Industrial Estate, Dublin 22. The EPA's own records agree: its July 2026 site visit records that licensable activity commenced on 6 February 2026 while the site 'continues to be under development and is not yet operating at full capacity', and its night-time monitoring of 13-14 August 2026 found facility noise from site operations audible at nearby homes. This supports operation of the installation as built on 21 September 2026. Which of the four permitted ICT facility buildings are complete or in service is not established, completion of the whole development is not claimed, and no IT capacity is stated.

locator.precision: Site-centre point of the EPA-licensed DUB10 installation from the register's National Grid Reference N232304 E307760 (the applicant's 'Site Centre Point'), transformed from Irish Grid (TM75) to WGS84. It locates the campus at 3-4 Crag Avenue, not the Energy Centre, any ICT facility building, a footprint, an entrance or the installation boundary.
locator.identity_review: The EPA register and the applicant's application form give the same grid reference for the P1113 installation at Crag Avenue, Clondalkin Industrial Estate, Dublin 22, D22 Y921, the location named in the noise management plan and both 2026 EPA site visit reports. The transformed point lies 7-11 m from the national planning register points for the South Dublin data-centre permissions at 3-4 Crag Avenue (SD13A/0271, SD18A/0068, SD20A/0309 for the four ICT Facility buildings and SD23A/0158 for the revised energy centre), and 161-183 m from the 2026 permissions for ICT Facility 1 amendments and the generators between ICT Facilities 2 and 3. The EPA's noise report places the site between the Grand Canal (south) and the M50 (east and north-east), which matches. Read as ITM the eastings would fall far offshore, so Irish Grid is the only plausible reading.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The register gives a single site-centre grid reference at 1 m resolution with no stated survey accuracy for a campus of about 13.4 ha (site area 133,800 in the planning register record for SD20A/0309), so the offset to any building is unknown. The TM75-to-WGS84 operation is rated at 1 m; the alternative operation moves the point 2.2 m. Decimal places are arithmetic precision.

Microsoft's letter to the EPA of 22 September 2026 identifies the P1191-01 installation as Dub 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12 and 13, with eight generator yards. The other Microsoft installations on the campus (P1187-01 and P1190-01) and DUB14/DUB15 are not part of this project, and no IT capacity is stated.

status.summary: The EPA granted Edgeconnex Ireland Limited industrial emissions licence P1204-01 under seal on 3 September 2026 for the operation of an installation at Newcastle Road, Lucan, County Dublin that 'will include' energy centre ESSDUB97 (20 gas engines of 10.3 MWth) and two data centres, EDCDUB04 and EDCDUB05, with 48 back-up generators. This dated government record identifies the project, supporting announced status as of 3 September 2026. The EPA's Technical Committee states that the installation has planning permission from An Coimisiún Pleanála (South Dublin SD19A/0042 / ABP-305948-19 and SD21A/0042, among others), but those grants date from 2020 to 2023 and whether each remains in effect was not established, so permitted status is not asserted. The licence is not planning consent, and no site works, construction, completion or operation is claimed.

February 2027 is a forecast completion, not an observation; the building's position on the campus, capacity, start date and tenancy are not stated, and the 6 MW and 'fully leased' statements in the release apply to the first data center only.

locator.identity_review: The BD24-61043 permit point lies inside parcel 176-02-610-002, whose active owner record (NV LAS NAP 17 & 18 LLC) gives the same situs, 6240 W Maule Ave, about 155 m from the centroid; the pump-house permit at that address also lies inside it. The NAP 17 and NAP 18 owner lots (176-02-610-003 and -004, recorded the same day, 8 September 2025) fill the two interior rings of 176-02-610-002, so the three lots are treated as one development property. The second data-center permit BD25-00549 ('NAP 17', 6322 W Maule Ave) has its address point about 15 m south of the union on the Maule Avenue frontage.
